findings.title: No managed compute — all workloads on EOL on-premises infrastructure
findings.description: All compute runs on a single on-premises Solaris 10 host with Oracle WebLogic Server 10.3. No managed container orchestration (ECS/EKS), no serverless (Lambda), no Fargate.
findings.gap: No managed compute services in use. The application depends on unsupported infrastructure (Solaris 10, WebLogic 10.3, Java 5) with no path to elastic scaling or automated patching.
findings.recommendation: Replatform the application to run on managed compute (ECS/Fargate or Lambda). This requires upgrading to Java 17+ with Spring Boot and containerizing the application.

findings.title: Self-managed Oracle 11g database — no managed database services
findings.description: The application connects to a self-managed Oracle 11g database via raw JDBC (jdbc:oracle:thin:@dbprod01:1521:LOANDB). No managed database services (RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB) are in use.
findings.gap: Database is entirely self-managed on-premises Oracle 11g (EOL). No automated failover, no managed backups, no elastic scaling.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL or RDS PostgreSQL using AWS DMS. The application uses standard SQL, making migration straightforward.

findings.title: No workflow orchestration — all logic hardcoded in application
findings.description: The application has a two-step workflow (calculate loan payment then save to database) implemented entirely in the execute() method. No workflow orchestration service is in use. For the stateful-crud archetype, business-critical multi-step operations should use dedicated orchestration.
findings.gap: All workflow logic is hardcoded in a single method with no error handling, retry logic, or state management between steps.
findings.recommendation: When replatforming, evaluate whether loan submission workflows would benefit from Step Functions orchestration. For the current simple calculate+save flow, orchestration may not be warranted until the business domain grows.

findings.title: No messaging or streaming infrastructure
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure exists. The application uses purely synchronous HTTP request/response. For the stateful-crud archetype, state changes that cross service boundaries should use managed messaging for decoupling.
findings.gap: No messaging infrastructure for state change propagation. Loan application submissions have no event notification mechanism.
findings.recommendation: When modernizing, introduce EventBridge or SNS for loan application lifecycle events (submitted, approved, rejected) to enable downstream systems to react without tight coupling.

findings.title: No network security configuration
findings.description: No network security configuration exists in the repository. No VPC, no subnets, no security groups, no NACLs. The application runs on-premises with network security managed entirely outside this codebase.
findings.gap: No in-repo evidence of network segmentation, private subnets, or least-privilege security groups.
findings.recommendation: When migrating to AWS, deploy in a VPC with private subnets, security groups with least-privilege rules, and VPC endpoints for AWS service access.

findings.title: No managed API entry point
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, CloudFront, or any managed entry point exists. The application is exposed directly via WebLogic's built-in HTTP listener.
findings.gap: Direct service exposure with no managed entry point. No throttling, no request validation, no WAF protection.
findings.recommendation: When migrating to AWS, place an API Gateway or ALB in front of the application with throttling, request validation, and WAF integration.

findings.title: No auto-scaling configured
findings.description: No auto-scaling mechanisms exist. The application runs on a single Solaris host with static capacity.
findings.gap: All capacity is statically provisioned on a single host. No ability to respond to traffic spikes or scale down during low demand.
findings.recommendation: When migrating to managed compute, configure auto-scaling with appropriate min/max thresholds.

findings.title: No backup and recovery configuration
findings.description: No backup configuration found in the repository. No aws_backup_plan, no backup_retention_period, no PITR configuration.
findings.gap: No evidence of automated backups, retention policies, or tested restore procedures for the Oracle 11g database.
findings.recommendation: When migrating to Aurora/RDS, enable automated backups with PITR and define retention periods. Test restore procedures.

findings.title: Zero Infrastructure as Code coverage
findings.description: No IaC exists in the repository. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, or any other IaC tool. All infrastructure is manually provisioned.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage. All infrastructure is created manually. No reproducibility, no environment consistency, no disaster recovery automation.
findings.recommendation: Adopt IaC (CDK or Terraform) for all AWS infrastructure when migrating. Define compute, networking, database, and operational resources in code.

findings.title: No CI/CD automation — all deployments manual
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Deployment is performed by manual WAR upload via the WebLogic admin console. No automated build, test, or deploy stages.
findings.gap: No automated build, test, or deploy stages. All deployments are manual, error-prone, and non-reproducible.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD with CodePipeline + CodeBuild or GitHub Actions. Include automated build, test, security scan, and deploy stages.

findings.title: Compound legacy language/framework — Java 5 with Struts 1.x
findings.description: The application is written in Java 5 with Apache Struts 1.3 framework. Java 5 is ancient (released 2004, EOL). Struts 1.x reached end of life in 2013 with known critical CVEs. No AWS SDK is present.
findings.gap: Compound legacy signals — Java 5 (ancient EOL version) AND Struts 1.x (EOL framework) AND no AWS SDK. Requires version upgrade, framework replacement, and SDK addition.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to Java 17+ with Spring Boot 3.x and AWS SDK v2. This is a prerequisite for all other modernization work.

findings.title: Tightly coupled monolith with no module boundaries
findings.description: The entire application logic exists in a single Action class. Business logic, data access, and presentation concerns are mixed in one method. No service interfaces, no module separation.
findings.gap: Pervasive shared state, no clear module boundaries, single deployable WAR with all concerns co-located. Cannot independently scale, deploy, or evolve any part.
findings.recommendation: See Decomposition Strategy. Begin with replatforming to Spring Boot with clear separation of concerns, then evaluate selective service extraction.

findings.title: All communication synchronous — no async patterns
findings.description: All communication is synchronous HTTP with no async patterns. No message queues, no event publishing, no async processing. For the stateful-crud archetype, cross-service state propagation should use async patterns.
findings.gap: All communication is synchronous HTTP with zero async patterns. State changes have no event-driven notification mechanism.
findings.recommendation: When modernizing, introduce async event publishing for loan application state changes using EventBridge or SNS.

findings.title: No async job handling capability
findings.description: All operations are handled synchronously regardless of duration. The application has no async job infrastructure, no status polling, no callback patterns.
findings.gap: No async infrastructure exists. The architecture cannot accommodate long-running operations without blocking the HTTP thread.
findings.recommendation: When modernizing, implement async job handling with status polling for operations that may exceed 30 seconds. Use SQS + Lambda or Step Functions.

findings.title: No API versioning strategy
findings.description: No API versioning strategy exists. The single endpoint /loan has no version prefix, no version header. Breaking changes would be deployed directly.
findings.gap: No versioning — any API change affects all consumers simultaneously.
findings.recommendation: When replatforming, implement URL-based versioning (e.g., /v1/loan) on all API endpoints.

findings.title: All service endpoints hardcoded in source
findings.description: All service endpoints are hardcoded in application code. The database connection string is a static constant in the Java source file. No service discovery mechanism.
findings.gap: All endpoints hardcoded in source code. Configuration changes require code recompilation and redeployment.
findings.recommendation: Externalize all service endpoints to environment variables or AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.

findings.title: No managed object storage for unstructured data
findings.description: No managed object storage (S3) is in use. The application stores loan application data in an Oracle database table only. No document storage or parsing pipeline.
findings.gap: No S3 or managed object storage. If loan documents exist, they are stored outside this system with no managed access.
findings.recommendation: When modernizing, store loan documents in S3 with lifecycle policies. Implement Textract for document parsing if applicable.

findings.title: No data access layer — raw JDBC in controller
findings.description: No data access layer exists. Raw JDBC calls are made directly in the Struts Action class with DriverManager.getConnection() per request. No connection pooling, no repository pattern.
findings.gap: Database access logic completely mixed with business logic and controller logic. No centralized data access pattern.
findings.recommendation: When replatforming to Spring Boot, implement a proper layered architecture: Controller → Service → Repository.

findings.title: Database engine past EOL with no version management
findings.description: Oracle 11g is well past end of life. No version pinning in IaC (no IaC exists). The database engine version is documented only in README.
findings.gap: Database engine past EOL with known security vulnerabilities and no patches. No version management strategy.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to a supported database engine. Aurora PostgreSQL provides fully managed, auto-patching database with Multi-AZ failover.

findings.title: No encryption at rest for sensitive data
findings.description: No encryption at rest configuration found. The Oracle 11g database has no in-repo evidence of encryption. No KMS keys configured.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest for sensitive loan application data (applicant names, financial details).
findings.recommendation: When migrating to Aurora/RDS, enable encryption at rest with a customer-managed KMS key.

findings.title: Legacy container-managed auth — no token-based authentication
findings.description: The application uses request.getRemoteUser() indicating container-managed authentication via WebLogic. Not modern token-based auth (OAuth2/JWT).
findings.gap: Authentication exists but uses legacy container-managed mechanisms with no standard token validation or centralized identity integration.
findings.recommendation: When modernizing, implement OAuth2/JWT authentication via Amazon Cognito. Use API Gateway authorizers for token validation.

findings.title: No centralized identity provider integration
findings.description: No centralized identity provider integration detected. Authentication handled entirely by WebLogic's built-in security realm. No Cognito, no OIDC, no SAML.
findings.gap: Application manages authentication entirely with no external IdP integration. No SSO capability.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito as centralized IdP. Enable SSO via SAML/OIDC federation.

findings.title: Plaintext credentials hardcoded in source code
findings.description: Database credentials are hardcoded as static constants: DB_USER='loan_app' and DB_PASS='loanApp2010'. Committed to version control and visible to anyone with repository access.
findings.gap: Plaintext credentials hardcoded in source code. Critical security vulnerability — credentials exposed in version control history permanently.
findings.recommendation: Remove hardcoded credentials immediately. Use AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation for all database credentials.

findings.title: No compute hardening or patching strategy
findings.description: No patching strategy or vulnerability scanning. All runtime components (Solaris 10, WebLogic 10.3, Java 5, Struts 1.x) are past end of life with known critical vulnerabilities.
findings.gap: No patching strategy, no vulnerability scanning, no hardened images. All runtime components EOL with known critical CVEs.
findings.recommendation: When migrating to AWS, use managed compute (Fargate/Lambda) for automatic OS patching. Enable Inspector for vulnerability scanning.

findings.title: No application security pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning tools configured. No SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, or container scanning. No CI/CD pipeline exists to integrate security tools into.
findings.gap: No security scanning in any form. SQL injection vulnerabilities and Struts 1.x critical CVEs go undetected.
findings.recommendation: When implementing CI/CD, integrate SAST, dependency scanning, and container scanning with security gates.

findings.title: No distributed tracing
findings.description: No distributed tracing instrumented. No OpenTelemetry SDK, no X-Ray, no trace ID propagation.
findings.gap: No tracing — debugging production issues requires log diving or reproducing in UAT.
findings.recommendation: When modernizing, instrument with OpenTelemetry SDK and export traces to X-Ray.

findings.title: No SLO definitions
findings.description: No SLO definitions found. No CloudWatch alarms, no latency/error-rate thresholds, no availability targets.
findings.gap: No formal definition of acceptable service levels.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for loan calculator availability and latency. Implement CloudWatch alarms on thresholds.

findings.title: No business metrics published
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business metrics (loan applications submitted, approval rates). No CloudWatch custom metrics.
findings.gap: No business outcome metrics. Cannot measure business value delivery.
findings.recommendation: When modernizing, publish custom CloudWatch metrics for business events: loans_submitted, loans_approved, calculation_errors.

findings.title: No anomaly detection or alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no incident notification integration.
findings.gap: No alerting — errors and outages go undetected until users report them.
findings.recommendation: When migrating to AWS, configure CloudWatch alarms with anomaly detection. Integrate with PagerDuty or OpsGenie.

findings.title: No automated tests of any kind
findings.description: No integration tests exist. No test files found. Testing is performed manually in a shared UAT environment.
findings.gap: No automated tests — no unit tests, no integration tests, no API tests. Regression risk during any modification is unmanaged.
findings.recommendation: When replatforming, implement integration tests for the loan calculation workflow. Add tests to CI pipeline as quality gates.

findings.title: No observability ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership defined. No CODEOWNERS for monitoring, no per-service dashboards, no alarm ownership.
findings.gap: No observability ownership — monitoring (if any) is ad hoc with no team attribution.
findings.recommendation: When modernizing, define observability ownership with per-service dashboards and named alarm owners.
